name: Genius RF

card.summary: A clinic radiofrequency microneedling device that remodels skin to smooth texture, scars and fine lines.
card.note: Clinic-delivered; results and downtime vary by settings and provider.

quick.overview:
Genius RF is Lutronic's radiofrequency microneedling system, cleared by the FDA in 2019. Fine insulated needles deliver energy into the dermis.

People use it to improve skin texture, acne scars and mild laxity, usually as a series of clinic sessions.
quick.mechanism: Insulated needles enter the skin to a set depth and release RF energy at the tips, heating the dermis to prompt collagen and elastin remodeling. Real-time feedback adjusts delivery.
quick.risks: Treatment is performed by clinicians; temporary redness and swelling are typical of microneedling procedures, and outcomes depend on provider and settings.

lead: Genius RF is a radiofrequency microneedling platform made by Lutronic. A handpiece with fine insulated needles enters the skin and delivers radiofrequency energy at the needle tips in the dermis. People use it to work on skin texture, fine lines, laxity and acne scars, the features that shape how smooth and firm the face and jawline look. [1][2]

The platform was cleared by the US FDA for radiofrequency microneedling in early 2019 and is described as the successor to Lutronic's Infini device. [1][3] Its maker highlights real-time feedback in which sensors and algorithms adjust energy delivery during treatment according to age, skin type, sun-exposure history, treatment site and tissue thickness. [1]

Clinics offer it as a series of in-office sessions. In looksmaxxing circles, RF microneedling is discussed as a skin-quality step alongside lasers and peels. Independent human trial data specific to this device are limited.

chain: Insulated needles deliver RF heat deep in the dermis
Controlled injury prompts new collagen and elastin
Smoother texture, softer scars and firmer lower face over a series of sessions
angle.text: Genius RF is used in clinics to improve skin quality and tighten skin. Providers list wrinkles, acne scars and laxity as targets, and say results build over several sessions.

paras: The handpiece carries a tip of sterile insulated needles. The needles penetrate to a set depth and the energy is released at their tips, so heating is concentrated in the dermis. [1][3] Lutronic says sensing and feedback algorithms keep energy delivery consistent and allow settings to be tailored by skin type, area and tissue thickness. [1]

Proponents say the controlled heat triggers new collagen and elastin formation, which is the basis for the smoother, firmer result. [1] Plain microneedling, the parent technique, is described by Wikipedia as repeatedly puncturing the skin with tiny sterile needles to stimulate collagen. [4]

Providers list wrinkles, acne scars and skin laxity as targets, and some state it suits a range of skin tones because of adjustable settings. [3] Dermatologist E. Victor Ross of Scripps Clinic called Genius Lutronic's strongest system and highlighted its real-time feedback, a quiet motor and an ergonomic handpiece. [1]

Wikipedia's microneedling article reports public-health concern when needling is done in non-medical settings without infection control; in April 2024 the CDC reported three women diagnosed with HIV after microneedling-based 'vampire facials' at an Albuquerque spa. That case concerned an unlicensed spa, not Genius RF. [4]

No studies found specific to the Genius RF platform in the peer-reviewed sources consulted. Manufacturer and clinic materials describe collagen remodelling and improved skin quality as the intended outcome. [1][3]

timeline.event: FDA clearance of Genius for radiofrequency microneedling announced (February 2019 coverage). [1]
